title: Differential session fingerprint merge for cost-boundary detection
creator: Rajat Mehra
description:
Context: We continue to see small groups of interleaved, asynchronous requests from long-lived sessions produce duplicate or split token attributions across tenant billing windows. This ticket implements a 'differential session fingerprint merge' stage in the ingest pipeline that correlates ephemeral session fragments into a single canonical session event for cost boundary evaluation and per-tenant chargeback.

Goal: Reduce duplicate token accounting and late-arrival leakage by building a deterministic, low-latency fingerprint merge that: 1) runs in the real-time ingest path before windowed aggregation, 2) tolerates partial identifiers (missing cookies/headers) using probabilistic joins, and 3) emits provenance metadata so downstream billing reconciliers can apply confidence scores. This should materially reduce billing disputes and post-billing reconciliations.

Approach:
- Design a lightweight canonicalization algorithm that combines: tenant_id, route_id, truncated KV-cache session id (if present), source_ip bucket, and time-bucketed N-gram of request timestamps. Use a salted HMAC to derive a stable fingerprint per tenant.
- Implement a streaming operator in the ingest Kafka consumer (go-service) that: generates fingerprint, performs local LRU cache of recent fingerprints to collapse duplicates, and tags events with fingerprint_confidence (high|medium|low).
- For low-confidence merges, emit both original event and a candidate merged event to a secondary topic flagged for offline reconciliation.
- Add metric instrumentation (histograms for merge latency, counters for merges by confidence, sampled traces) and a dashboard for monitoring false-merge rates and late-arrival corrections.

Non-goals: This ticket does not rework the ledger schema or billing price calculations. It only changes attribution inputs to existing aggregation jobs. A follow-up will add automatic correction heuristics in the reconciler if needed.

Acceptance criteria:
- New fingerprint is generated for >=98% of ingest events in staging and latency adds <3ms p95 to the ingest path.
- Duplicate attributions measured on a controlled test harness reduced by >=75% for interleaved session cases.
- Downstream aggregation jobs accept the new fingerprint metadata without schema migration (backwards-compatible fields).
- Monitoring dashboards and alerting for high false-merge rates deployed to console and included in runbook.

Out-of-band artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/SESSION-FINGERPRINT-MERGE, prototype notebook with synthetic harness: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/fingerprint-proto, draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/642
acceptance_criteria: Fingerprint generated for >=98% of events in staging
Duplicate attributions reduced by >=75% in test harness
Downstream jobs accept fingerprint metadata with no schema break
Dashboards and alerts deployed with runbook entries
technical_notes: Algorithm: tenant-salted HMAC over concatenated canonical fields, truncated to 128 bits; rotated salt stored in KMS and versioned in event metadata
Cache: bounded LRU in the ingest consumer with asynchronous eviction metrics; consider mempool backpressure if consumer lags
Confidence: deterministic rules (cookie+session_id present => high), probabilistic score using bloom-filter hits and timestamp sketch => medium/low
Fallback: write original event id into 'merge_candidates' topic for downstream offline reconciler
Privacy: no PII stored in fingerprint; IP used as /24 bucket only; design reviewed with security team
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout in staging cluster (1 consumer shard) for 48h
Shadow mode in production for 72h (generate fingerprint, do not change downstream routing)
Canary enable for 10% ingest traffic and monitor merge/false-merge metrics for 48h
Full enable with automated rollback if false-merge rate >0.5% or merge latency >5ms p95
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboard: Console > Metering > Fingerprint Merge (merge_rate, false_merge_rate, merge_latency_p50_p95),
migration_steps: Coordinate with aggregation owners to accept new 'session_fingerprint' and 'fingerprint_confidence' fields (backward-compatible)
Deploy ingest change in shadow mode and verify aggregations unchanged
Run 7-day parallel roll comparing billing outputs from canonical pipeline vs shadowed pipeline and quantify divergence
If divergence <0.1% apply full enable and retire 'merge_candidates' topic after 14 days
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false merges causing underbilling => Mitigation: conservative confidence rules and initial shadow-only rollout
Risk: increased ingest latency => Mitigation: microbenchmark HMAC implementation in native go and pre-warm salt cache
Risk: cache thrashing under bursty traffic => Mitigation: adaptive LRU sizing based on consumer lag metrics
comments: 2025-03-11 Rajat Mehra: Initial write-up done. Shared design doc with billing and security teams. Security requested IP bucketing and no persistent PII - incorporated.
2025-03-12 Lina Garcia (Billing): Agreed on emitting confidence scores so reconciler can weight merges. Asked for a synthetic harness to validate dispute reduction.
2025-03-13 Ava Thompson: Prototype implemented HMAC fingerprint and local LRU, p95 overhead ~1.8ms in microbench. Preparing PR for review.
2025-03-15 PR Review (infra): raised concern about KMS salt rotation frequency. Decided to version salt every 30 days and include salt_version in event metadata.

2025-03-17 QA (Suresh Patel): Ran synthetic interleaved session test with 10M events; duplicates reduced 82%. Observed a small spike in low-confidence merges for one client - filed follow-up ENG-332110 to tune heuristics.
2025-03-18 PM check-in (Maya Chen): Confirmed rollout cadence and asked for billing-owner signoff before canary. Billing owner Lina to approve after 7-day parallel report.
